name: @mmerterden/multi-agent-mcp

tools.name: ios_list_devices
tools.description: List all available iOS simulators and their state. Use it first to pick a UDID; ios_boot_device starts one.

tools.name: ios_boot_device
tools.description: Boot an iOS simulator by UDID or name. Use it when ios_list_devices shows no booted simulator.

tools.name: ios_screenshot
tools.description: Capture an iOS simulator screenshot. Without `path` the image comes back inline, downscaled to 800 px on the longest side as a quality-80 JPEG (~60 KB instead of the ~3 MB full-resolution PNG, which is ~4 MB as base64 on every capture); `format: "png"` with `max_width: 0` returns the original PNG bytes. The full-resolution PNG stays on disk either way. Pass `path` to write the full-resolution PNG there and return only its location, which is what a run taking many captures needs - and what design-check and ios_visual_diff read. Withheld (PIXEL_TAINTED) after a secret_ref was typed on the simulator, until an app is launched or terminated. Use when you need to see the screen, or to collect captures for a later comparison.

allow_secret_pixels.description: Capture even though a secret was typed on this target since its last reset (the capture may show it). Default false: the screenshot is withheld with PIXEL_TAINTED.

path.description: Absolute file path to write the PNG to. The parent directory must already exist. Returns the path instead of the image.

max_width.description: Longest side of the inline image in pixels (default 800). 0 keeps the original size. Ignored with `path`.

format.description: Inline image format (default jpeg). Ignored with `path`.

quality.description: JPEG quality 1-100 (default 80). Ignored for png and with `path`.

tools.name: ios_tap
tools.description: Tap at coordinates on iOS simulator. Prefer ios_tap_element; use coordinates only for targets with no label or id.

tools.name: ios_swipe
tools.description: Swipe on iOS simulator. Use it for scrolling and drags in points; on Android use android_swipe.

tools.name: ios_tap_element
tools.description: Tap the element a locator names on the iOS simulator, at its centre, instead of guessing coordinates. Reads the screen with idb ui describe-all. Zero matches fails with LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND (with near misses as suggestions when the screen has similar text), several with LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS listing the candidates (id, label, frame) so the locator can be refined. Prefer it over ios_tap; check a locator first with ui_locate.

locator.description: What to find. At least one of id, role, label, text, value. Several fields must all match.

id.description: Accessibility identifier (iOS), resource-id with or without the package prefix (Android), data-testid or id attribute (web). Exact.

role.description: Role or type: button, textbox, text, image, switch, checkbox, cell, link ... or the platform spelling (Button, AXButton, android.widget.EditText).

text.description: Visible text: matches the label, the text or the value.

value.description: Current value, e.g. what a text field holds.

exact.description: Default true. false makes label, text and value case-insensitive substring matches.

index.description: Pick the Nth match (0-based) on purpose when several match.

verify.description: Re-read the screen just before the tap and check the element is still there and on top (ui_target_check). A shifted element is tapped at its new centre; a covered one fails with TARGET_OCCUPIED naming what covers it, a vanished one with TARGET_DISAPPEARED. Retries twice, 400 ms apart, for an animation to settle. Costs one extra screen read. Default false.

tools.name: ios_type_element
tools.description: Tap the element a locator names to focus it, then type text or a secret_ref into it. Zero matches fails with LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND (with near misses as suggestions when the screen has similar text), several with LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS listing the candidates (id, label, frame) so the locator can be refined. Prefer it over ios_type_text when the field has a locator.

locator.description: What to find. At least one of id, role, label, text, value. Several fields must all match.

id.description: Accessibility identifier (iOS), resource-id with or without the package prefix (Android), data-testid or id attribute (web). Exact.

role.description: Role or type: button, textbox, text, image, switch, checkbox, cell, link ... or the platform spelling (Button, AXButton, android.widget.EditText).

text.description: Visible text: matches the label, the text or the value.

value.description: Current value, e.g. what a text field holds.

exact.description: Default true. false makes label, text and value case-insensitive substring matches.

index.description: Pick the Nth match (0-based) on purpose when several match.

secret_ref.description: Logical key of a secret to type instead of text. Resolved through the credential store (credential-store.sh get <key>) or MULTI_AGENT_MCP_SECRET_<KEY>; the value is typed but masked as <secret:key> in every result, and screenshots of the target are withheld afterwards. A key nobody onboarded fails with CREDENTIAL_MISSING.

A shifted element is tapped at its new centre; a covered one fails with TARGET_OCCUPIED naming what covers it, a vanished one with TARGET_DISAPPEARED. Retries twice, 400 ms apart, for an animation to settle. Costs one extra screen read. Default false.

tools.name: ios_type_text
tools.description: Type text on iOS simulator into the focused field. Pass secret_ref instead of text for a password or token: it is typed but never echoed. Use it once a field has focus; ios_type_element focuses and types in one call.

secret_ref.description: Logical key of a secret to type instead of text. Resolved through the credential store (credential-store.sh get <key>) or MULTI_AGENT_MCP_SECRET_<KEY>; the value is typed but masked as <secret:key> in every result, and screenshots of the target are withheld afterwards. A key nobody onboarded fails with CREDENTIAL_MISSING.

tools.name: ios_launch_app
tools.description: Launch iOS app by bundle ID. On Android use android_launch_app.

tools.name: ios_terminate_app
tools.description: Terminate iOS app. Use it to restart the app cleanly; ios_go_home only backgrounds it.

tools.name: ios_list_apps
tools.description: List installed iOS apps. Use it to confirm an install or find a bundle id for ios_launch_app.

tools.name: ios_go_home
tools.description: Press iOS home button. Leaves the app running; to end it use ios_terminate_app.

tools.name: ios_set_appearance
tools.description: Set iOS light/dark mode. On Android use android_set_dark_mode.

tools.name: ios_set_content_size
tools.description: Set iOS Dynamic Type size for accessibility testing. On Android use android_set_font_scale.

tools.name: ios_set_locale
tools.description: Change iOS app language (requires restart). On Android use android_set_locale.

language.description: Language code (e.g. tr, en, de, ar)

tools.name: ios_open_url
tools.description: Open URL or deep link on iOS. Use it to open a screen by deep link instead of tapping through the app.

tools.name: ios_status_bar
tools.description: Override iOS status bar. Use 'preset' for App Store screenshot defaults (clean=9:41/100%, testing=11:11/50%, low-battery=20%, airplane=offline) or 'clear' to revert. Manual time/battery_level override the preset. Use it before ios_screenshot for store captures.

tools.name: ios_push_notification
tools.description: Send simulated iOS push notification. Use it for notification handling without a push server.

tools.name: ios_grant_permission
tools.description: Grant iOS privacy permission. Use it before launch to skip the permission alert; ios_revoke_permission undoes it.

tools.name: ios_revoke_permission
tools.description: Revoke iOS privacy permission. Use it to test the denied path; ios_grant_permission reverses it.

tools.name: ios_reset_permissions
tools.description: Reset all iOS permissions for an app. Use it to see first-run permission alerts again; ios_revoke_permission targets one service.

tools.name: ios_set_location
tools.description: Set simulated iOS GPS location. Clear it with ios_clear_location; on Android use android_set_location.

tools.name: ios_clear_location
tools.description: Clear simulated iOS location. Use it after ios_set_location to drop the simulated position.

tools.name: ios_set_increase_contrast
tools.description: Enable/disable iOS Increase Contrast. Pair with design_contrast_check for ratios computed from colours and tokens.

tools.name: ios_record_video
tools.description: Record the iOS simulator screen. action:"start" (default) spawns `simctl io recordVideo` in the background and returns immediately; action:"stop" ends the recording and returns the video file path. One recording per device. For a still frame use ios_screenshot; media_frames pulls key frames out of the video.

filename.description: Output file name or absolute path (start only). Default rec_<timestamp>.mp4 in the tool's temp dir.

allow_secret_pixels.description: Capture even though a secret was typed on this target since its last reset (the capture may show it). Default false: the screenshot is withheld with PIXEL_TAINTED.

tools.name: ios_add_media
tools.description: Add photo/video to iOS photo library. Use it to seed the photo library, for example with a document_generate fixture.

tools.name: ios_keychain_reset
tools.description: Reset iOS simulator keychain. Use it for a signed-out first launch; ios_erase_device resets everything.

tools.name: ios_get_app_container
tools.description: Get iOS app container path. Use it to read the files, databases and defaults the app wrote.

tools.name: ios_erase_device
tools.description: Factory reset iOS simulator. Wipes every app and setting; for one app use ios_reset_permissions or ios_keychain_reset.

tools.name: ios_get_ui_tree
tools.description: Get iOS accessibility UI tree via macOS AX APIs. Pass `path` to write the raw dump to a file and return only its location - the full tree can be tens of KB. With `since`, the reply is JSON with a snapshot_id over the element list ui_locate reads (idb when installed): only the added, removed and changed nodes relative to that earlier read, with stable node ids, or the full list when it is unknown (since:"none" for a first baseline). For one element use ui_locate; to act on an element by identity use ios_tap_element.

since.description: snapshot_id of an earlier read to diff against.

path.description: Absolute file path to write the raw tree JSON to. The parent directory must already exist.

tools.name: ios_accessibility_audit
tools.description: Audit iOS app accessibility on the booted simulator: missing labels, controls a screen reader cannot name, tap targets under 44pt, missing identifiers, and whether the reading order follows the visual layout. Reports measurable:false with a reason rather than a clean result when the tree could not be read - booting a device is not enough, Simulator.app must be running. Scopes to the device screen, never the simulator own chrome. For Apple's own audit (contrast, Dynamic Type) use ios_accessibility_audit_deep; on Android use android_accessibility_audit.

scope.description: Filter: only audit elements whose identifier starts with this prefix (e.g. 'login_', 'settings_'). Omit to audit all.

rtl.description: Expect right-to-left reading within a row. Default false.

tools.name: ios_biometric
tools.description: Simulate Face ID / Touch ID on iOS simulator (match or nomatch). Use it for the Face ID and Touch ID success and failure paths.

tools.name: ios_archive_audit
tools.description: DEPRECATED - use ios_app_store_audit (18-rule deep scan). Lighter 6-check audit kept for backward compatibility only.

tools.name: ios_export_ipa
tools.description: Export a .xcarchive to a signed .ipa via xcodebuild -exportArchive. Generates the exportOptions.plist from the arguments (method defaults to app-store-connect), so callers do not have to hand-maintain one. Returns the .ipa path plus parsed errors; a run that exits 0 without producing an .ipa is reported as a failure. Pair with ios_testflight_validate for the pre-submission gate.

method.description: Export method: app-store-connect (default) | release-testing | enterprise | development

provisioning_profiles.description: Map of bundleId -> provisioning profile name (manual signing)

allow_provisioning_updates.description: Off by default. Lets xcodebuild register devices and create/modify provisioning profiles in the developer account - a change on Apple's side, so it is opt-in

tools.name: ios_testflight_validate
tools.description: Run Apple's own pre-submission validation on an .ipa via `xcrun altool --validate-app`, then map returned ITMS error codes onto the App Store rule each one implies. This is the authoritative gate: unlike the static ios_app_store_audit it can catch an unregistered bundle ID, a profile that does not match the App Store Connect app record, a version+build pair already used, and entitlements not provisioned for the app ID. Auth is a 3-tier chain: ASC API key (api_key_id + api_issuer_id, or with neither api_key_id nor apple_id given the key onboarded for the store_* tools, whose .p8 is written to a private temporary file for the call), else Apple ID + app-specific password referenced indirectly through a keychain item or env var (never passed by value), else the gate returns verdict SKIPPED with a reason. SKIPPED is not a pass - it means Apple was never asked. Set list_providers=true for a pre-flight that reports which teams the credentials can deliver for (needed when a corporate Apple ID belongs to several).

api_key_id.description: App Store Connect API key ID (tier 1)

p8_path.description: Explicit path to AuthKey_<id>.p8; otherwise altool's search dirs are used

keychain_item.description: Keychain item holding the app-specific password (tier 2, preferred)

password_env_var.description: Env var holding the app-specific password (tier 2 fallback)

provider_public_id.description: Required when the account belongs to multiple providers

list_providers.description: Pre-flight only: list deliverable providers and return

tools.name: ios_app_store_audit
tools.description: Deep App Store Review compliance audit for .xcarchive bundles. 18-rule catalog covering privacy manifest, code signing, embedded SDKs, entitlements, asset hygiene, IPv6 compliance, debug-tool leak detection, Swift ABI compatibility, SDK floor (ITMS-90725), and more. Returns structured JSON with severity-ranked violations and ITMS error code mappings. Replaces ios_archive_audit (deprecated). Pass rules='core' for the 6 baseline checks (code-signing, entitlements, info-plist, privacy-manifest, binary-size, sdk-floor); 'all'|'deep' for the full 18-rule scan; CSV like 'binary-size,ipv6-compliance' for an explicit subset. A static archive check; pair with ios_testflight_validate for Apple's server-side verdict.

tools.name: ios_xcodebuild
tools.description: Build / test / clean an Xcode project with progressive disclosure. Returns one-line summary plus xcresult ID; drill in via ios_xcresult. Token-efficient - full log stays out of context unless requested.

destination.description: Xcode destination string. Default: generic iOS Simulator; for action test, the booted simulator (xcodebuild refuses a generic destination for test)

extra_args.description: Additional xcodebuild arguments. A string is split on space and tab and may hold only printable ASCII plain flags and values: shell metacharacters, glob characters, ~ and quotes are refused. A list of strings is passed as given, one argument per entry, so a value with a space, ~ or glob goes there ("OTHER_SWIFT_FLAGS=-D CI"). With MULTI_AGENT_UNATTENDED=1, any = (a NAME=value build-setting override included), -xcconfig, -toolchain, -xcroot, the provisioning and API-key flags, unvalidated plugin and macro flags, registry and SCM overrides, -IDE* defaults and an -sdk path are refused in either form, and so is a list entry padded with space or tab or a flag entry holding a space.

anyOf.patternHint: may contain only plain flags and values (no shell metacharacters ; & | ` $ ( ) { } < > \\)

tools.name: ios_xcresult
tools.description: Drill into a previous ios_xcodebuild result by xcresult ID. Modes: summary (counts), errors (file:line + message), warnings, log (last N lines), tests (failed), metrics (XCTMetric performance results as JSON). Use this instead of dumping the whole build log into context.

log_lines.description: Lines of raw log to return when mode=log (default 200)

test_id.description: mode=metrics only: scope to one test case or suite instead of every measured test

tools.name: ios_visual_diff
tools.description: Compare two PNG screenshots. Pixel mode (default) returns JSON with diff_pct, pass/fail vs threshold, an optional diff image and `regions`: boxes {x,y,w,h,cells,where} in baseline pixels where more than 2% of a grid cell differs, largest first; images of different sizes fail as size_mismatch. Layout mode compares structure instead of pixels: both images are reduced to edge maps at one shared width, compared over the height they share (the height difference is reported as height_delta_pct, not failed), and scored per grid cell, so a theme or colour change scores as a match while content that moved, appeared or vanished is flagged as regions; empty areas carry no weight. Verdict bands: >=90 matches, >=75 close, >=50 partly, else different. Use pixel mode for snapshot regression checks, layout mode across light/dark, devices or resolutions. For a Figma render against a device capture use design_visual_compare.

threshold.description: Pixel mode: per-pixel color threshold 0..1 (default 0.1, lower = stricter)

max_diff_pct.description: Pixel mode: fail if diff exceeds this percent (default 1.0)

output.description: Pixel mode: path to write diff PNG (optional)

min_score.description: Layout mode: pass at this score or above (default 90)

layout_width.description: Layout mode: shared width both images are scaled to (default 480)

layout_cols.description: Layout mode: grid columns of square cells (default 12)

edge_threshold.description: Layout mode: luma step that counts as an edge (default 40)

tools.name: ios_leaks
tools.description: Look for leaked memory in a running simulator (or host) process with /usr/bin/leaks. mode=snapshot reports the current leak count and bytes; mode=diff reports only leaks new since a saved memory graph, which is the shape a regression gate wants. Reports measurable:false when the target lacks get-task-allow rather than reporting it as clean - leaks exits 0 in that case, so an unmeasurable target and a clean one are indistinguishable by exit status. Debug builds are debuggable; Apple-signed apps are not. For Android memory use android_meminfo.

pid.description: Process id. Either this or bundle_id.

bundle_id.description: Bundle id of an app running on the booted simulator; its pid is resolved for you.

baseline_graph.description: mode=diff: path to the memory graph saved by an earlier call

output_graph.description: Save a memory graph here to use as a later baseline

tools.name: ios_accessibility_audit_deep
tools.description: Run Apple's own accessibility audit (XCUIAccessibilityAudit) through an existing XCUITest and report its findings: contrast, Dynamic Type, clipped text, traits, hit regions, element descriptions. These cannot be reached from an accessibility tree dump, which is why this is a separate tool from ios_accessibility_audit and does not replace it. It is an xcodebuild test run, minutes rather than seconds, and the named test MUST itself call performAccessibilityAudit() - a test that does not is indistinguishable from an audit that found nothing, so the result reports whether the test ran and never invents a clean verdict. Needs an XCUITest; for a quick check from the accessibility tree use ios_accessibility_audit.

project.description: Path to the .xcodeproj. Give this or workspace.

test_identifier.description: e.g. AuditTest/testAccessibilityAudit(). Omit to read every test that ran.

device_id.description: Simulator udid. Defaults to the booted one.

tools.name: ios_list_crashes
tools.description: List recent crash reports from the host's ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports - where simulator app crashes land. Filter by process name, bound by age and count. On Android use android_list_crashes.

app.description: Only reports whose file name (the crashed process) contains this substring

since_min.description: Only reports newer than this many minutes

tools.name: android_list_devices
tools.description: List connected Android devices and emulators. Use it first to get a device_id when more than one device is connected.

tools.name: android_screenshot
tools.description: Capture an Android screenshot. Without `path` the image comes back inline, downscaled to 800 px on the longest side as a quality-80 JPEG (~60 KB instead of a multi-MB full-resolution PNG on every capture); `format: "png"` with `max_width: 0` returns the original PNG bytes. Downscaling needs sips (macOS); without it the original PNG is returned and the result says so. Pass `path` to write the full-resolution PNG there and return only its location - what a multi-capture run and the design tools need. Withheld (PIXEL_TAINTED) after a secret_ref was typed on the device, until an app is launched or stopped. For a pixel comparison of two captures use ios_visual_diff; for element bounds use android_get_ui_tree.

allow_secret_pixels.description: Capture even though a secret was typed on this target since its last reset (the capture may show it). Default false: the screenshot is withheld with PIXEL_TAINTED.

path.description: Absolute file path to write the PNG to. The parent directory must already exist. Returns the path instead of the image.

max_width.description: Longest side of the inline image in pixels (default 800). 0 keeps the original size. Ignored with `path`.

format.description: Inline image format (default jpeg). Ignored with `path`.

quality.description: JPEG quality 1-100 (default 80). Ignored for png and with `path`.

tools.name: android_tap
tools.description: Tap at coordinates on Android. Prefer android_tap_element; use coordinates only for targets with no text or id.

tools.name: android_tap_sequence
tools.description: Tap 2 to 10 points on Android in one shell call, delay_ms apart (default 120, at most 2000). For a UI that closes before separate tap calls arrive: a menu opened by the first tap, a toast's action, a long-press popup. Coordinates in pixels, as android_tap. Use android_tap_element for a single element.

tools.name: android_swipe
tools.description: Swipe on Android. Use it for scrolling and drags in pixels; on iOS use ios_swipe.

tools.name: android_type_text
tools.description: Type text on Android via `adb shell input text`. The text reaches the device shell as a quoted literal, so shell characters are typed, not interpreted. Platform limit: `input text` drops non-ASCII characters and some symbols; use the keyboard for those. Pass secret_ref instead of text for a password or token: it is typed but never echoed. Use it once a field has focus; android_type_element focuses and types in one call.

secret_ref.description: Logical key of a secret to type instead of text. Resolved through the credential store (credential-store.sh get <key>) or MULTI_AGENT_MCP_SECRET_<KEY>; the value is typed but masked as <secret:key> in every result, and screenshots of the target are withheld afterwards. A key nobody onboarded fails with CREDENTIAL_MISSING.

tools.name: android_key_event
tools.description: Send Android key event (HOME=3, BACK=4, ENTER=66). For back and home use android_go_back and android_go_home.

tools.name: android_launch_app
tools.description: Launch Android app by package name. To measure start-up time use android_launch_time instead.

activity.description: Activity class, relative (.MainActivity) or fully qualified (com.example.MainActivity); started as package_name/activity. Omit to launch through the LAUNCHER intent.

tools.name: android_stop_app
tools.description: Force-stop Android app. Use it to restart cleanly; to also wipe data use android_clear_app_data.

tools.name: android_list_packages
tools.description: List installed Android packages. Use it to confirm an install or find a package name for android_launch_app.

tools.name: android_go_home
tools.description: Press Android home button. Leaves the app running; to end it use android_stop_app.

tools.name: android_go_back
tools.description: Press Android back button. For any other key use android_key_event.

tools.name: android_get_ui_tree
tools.description: Dump Android UI hierarchy (uiautomator XML with bounds, text, resource-id). The raw dump is unbounded; pass `path` to write it to a file instead of inlining, or filter:"interactive" for a compact JSON list of just the interactive elements (class, text, resource-id, center coords). With `since`, the reply is JSON with a snapshot_id: only the added, removed and changed nodes relative to that earlier read, with stable node ids, or the compact full list when it is unknown (since:"none" for a first baseline). For one element use ui_locate; to act on an element by identity use android_tap_element.

since.description: snapshot_id of an earlier read to diff against.

path.description: Absolute file path to write the dump to: the raw XML, or the filtered JSON when filter is set. The parent directory must already exist.

filter.description: interactive: return only clickable/focusable elements as compact JSON instead of the raw XML

tools.name: android_set_dark_mode
tools.description: Enable/disable Android dark mode. On iOS use ios_set_appearance.

tools.name: android_set_font_scale
tools.description: Set Android font scale (1.0=normal, 2.0=extra large). Use it for large-text layout checks; on iOS use ios_set_content_size.

tools.name: android_set_locale
tools.description: Set an app's locale (per-app locale, Android 13+/API 33). package_name is needed in practice: the per-app locale API is app-scoped, and device-wide locale change is not reachable over adb without root. On iOS use ios_set_locale.

package_name.description: Target app package. Without it the call returns an error instead of silently doing nothing.

tools.name: android_set_location
tools.description: Set mock Android GPS location. On iOS use ios_set_location.

tools.name: android_grant_permission
tools.description: Grant Android runtime permission. Use it before launch to skip the runtime dialog; android_revoke_permission undoes it.

tools.name: android_revoke_permission
tools.description: Revoke Android runtime permission. Use it to test the denied path; android_grant_permission reverses it.

tools.name: android_record_screen
tools.description: Record the Android screen. action:"start" (default) spawns `adb shell screenrecord` in the background and returns immediately; action:"stop" ends the recording, pulls the file off the device and returns its local path. One recording per device; screenrecord hard-caps a segment at 180s. For a still frame use android_screenshot; media_frames pulls key frames out of the recording.

duration.description: Time limit in seconds (start only, max 180, default 180)

path.description: Local file path to pull the recording to (start only). Default rec_<timestamp>.mp4 in the tool's temp dir.

allow_secret_pixels.description: Capture even though a secret was typed on this target since its last reset (the capture may show it). Default false: the screenshot is withheld with PIXEL_TAINTED.

tools.name: android_install_apk
tools.description: Install APK on Android. Use it for a local build; for Google's check of an .aab use store_play_validate_bundle.

tools.name: android_uninstall_app
tools.description: Uninstall Android app. Use it for a clean reinstall; to keep the app and reset its data use android_clear_app_data.

tools.name: android_logcat
tools.description: Get Android logcat entries. For crash stacks alone use android_list_crashes.

tools.name: android_get_screen_size
tools.description: Get Android screen resolution. Use it to scale coordinates for android_tap and android_swipe.

tools.name: android_open_url
tools.description: Open URL or deep link on Android. Use it to open a screen by deep link instead of tapping through the app.

tools.name: android_clear_app_data
tools.description: Clear all data for Android app. Use it for a first-launch state; to only stop the process use android_stop_app.

tools.name: android_accessibility_audit
tools.description: Audit Android app accessibility on the connected device: missing contentDescription, clickable nodes TalkBack cannot focus, touch targets under 48dp, missing resource-ids, and whether the reading order follows the visual layout. Reports measurable:false with a reason rather than a clean result when the dump could not be read. On iOS use ios_accessibility_audit; for colour contrast use design_contrast_check.

scope.description: Filter: only audit elements whose resource-id contains this prefix (e.g. 'login_', 'com.example:id/login_'). Omit to audit all.

rtl.description: Expect right-to-left reading within a row. Default false.

tools.name: android_launch_time
tools.description: Measure Android app launch time: force-stops the package, starts it with am start -W, and reports TotalTime/WaitTime in ms plus the platform's own LaunchState (COLD/WARM/HOT). Below Android 10 there is no LaunchState and cold_start is null rather than assumed. Use it when start-up time is the question; android_launch_app only starts the app.

activity.description: Activity class, relative (.MainActivity) or fully qualified (com.example.MainActivity); started as package_name/activity. Default .MainActivity.

tools.name: android_apk_audit
tools.description: Audit APK/AAB for Play Store compliance: debug flag, target SDK, permissions, signing, ProGuard. A local static check; for Google's own validation of an .aab use store_play_validate_bundle.

tools.name: android_meminfo
tools.description: Read an Android app's memory via `adb shell dumpsys meminfo` (KB, no root). mode=snapshot returns the App Summary rows and totals; mode=diff compares two snapshots so growth across the same flow is visible, which is the signal a leak actually produces - a single absolute number says almost nothing. Reports measurable:false when the package has no running process rather than returning zeros. For iOS memory use ios_leaks.

baseline_json.description: mode=diff: the JSON returned by an earlier snapshot call

tools.name: android_list_crashes

tools.name: web_session_open
tools.description: Open an isolated browser session (its own context: page, cookies, storage, console and network) so parallel callers do not drive one page. Pass the returned id as `session` to any web_* tool. At most MULTI_AGENT_MCP_WEB_MAX_SESSIONS sessions (default 4), the default session included. mode:attach connects to a Chrome the user started with --remote-debugging-port and a separate --user-data-dir (Chrome 136+ ignores the port on the default profile); mode:profile launches the installed Chrome, visible, on a persistent profile directory the user logs in to once; the server starts that browser, so it reports navigator.webdriver=true, while an attached browser the user started does not. Both act with the user's own logins: submits, committing clicks (send, pay, apply, post...), Enter in a form field, uploads, web_eval and WebMCP calls return a preview until repeated with confirm:true, they cannot run inside agent_run_steps, and tools that reach the whole profile (storage state, routes, clock, offline, crawl, trace) are refused. A captcha or a login wall is the user's to clear. Sites such as LinkedIn forbid automated access in their terms and may restrict an account that uses it. Use it for parallel callers or the user's signed-in Chrome; otherwise the default session of web_goto is enough.

session.description: Id to use, 1-40 letters, digits, dashes or underscores. Omit for a generated one.

record_video.description: launch only: record the session as <out_dir>/<session>.webm, finalised by web_session_close (more pages as <session>.2.webm). out_dir absolute and under the read deny list policy, a name already there is never replaced; size WIDTHxHEIGHT 320-1920 a side; max_mb 1-500, default 200 and max_seconds 10-1800, default 300: a recording over its time or its folder's size ends the session at the next call with a note (over the size cap it is discarded). The files are finalised on close and at shutdown; whatever is left at exit is deleted, and a folder a killed process left behind is swept at the next open or start. A session a secret was typed in (secret_ref) has its whole video discarded, unless allow_secret_pixels is true.

mode.description: launch (default): a fresh headless context. attach / profile: the user's real Chrome, see the description.

headless_mode.description: launch only. shell (default): the bundled headless shell, fastest. new: full Chromium in new headless mode, for pages that behave differently in the shell (chromium only). headed: a visible window to watch the run; refused with MULTI_AGENT_UNATTENDED=1.

tools.name: web_crawl
tools.description: Follow same-origin links from `url` (or the current page), extracting each one and indexing it so context_search can rank the crawl afterwards. Bounded: max_pages default 20 (cap 200), max_depth default 2, one request at a time with a delay, robots.txt respected (Allow/Disallow, wildcards, Crawl-delay; a robots.txt that answers 5xx or does not answer stops the crawl, a 4xx or a 200 with no rule in it allows it, and the summary says which), and a self-identifying User-Agent. Scope with include_paths / exclude_paths regexes, seed from the sitemap, fold query strings, and write an llms.txt of the crawl. Use it for many pages of one site; for one page use web_scrape, for URLs only web_map.

url.description: Start here. Default: the current page.

index.description: Index each page into the full-text index. Default true - a crawl whose pages cannot be searched afterwards returns a wall of text nobody can query.

max_retries.description: Retries for a page that answers 429 or 503, honouring Retry-After (capped at 10s) or backing off with jitter. Default 2. A page still throttled after them stops the crawl.

tools.name: web_scrape
tools.description: Fetch one URL in a throwaway browser session and return it in the requested formats: markdown (main content by default), text, html, links, screenshot (file), selectors (structured JSON from {field: css} without a model), structured_data (JSON-LD blocks, microdata items, Open Graph and Twitter tags; a malformed JSON-LD block is listed in errors by position, the rest still returned) and change_tracking (new / same / changed / removed against the last scrape of this URL and tag, with a diff). Optional pre-extraction actions reuse web_click / web_type / web_press_key / web_wait_for / web_select_option / web_hover / web_fill_form. Results are cached on disk and shared: max_age_ms (default 2 days, 0 = always fetch), cache_only answers from the cache or fails. Page text is fenced as untrusted and scanned for prompt-injection shapes. Use it for one URL with no interaction; for a page you click through use web_goto, for many pages web_crawl.
