session.description: Web session id from web_session_open. Default: the default session.

tools.name: web_trace
tools.description: Record a Playwright trace of the session (actions, DOM snapshots, screenshots, network). stop writes trace.zip and returns its path; open it with `npx playwright show-trace <path>`. Use it when a failing flow needs a replayable record; for one frame use web_screenshot.

path.description: stop: absolute .zip path. Default: a file in the toolkit's work directory.

session.description: Web session id from web_session_open. Default: the default session.

tools.name: web_generate_locator
tools.description: Turn a ref from the latest web_snapshot into stable locators: Playwright code (getByTestId / getByRole / getByLabel / getByText) and the ui_locate locator object, each with how many elements it matches now. The first unique one is the recommendation, ready for a generated test or an agent_run_steps step.

session.description: Web session id from web_session_open. Default: the default session.

tools.name: web_assert_aria
tools.description: Assert the page (or a subtree) against an ARIA snapshot template in Playwright's YAML form, e.g. '- heading "Orders" [level=1]\n- button /Save|Kaydet/'. contain (default) lets the template list a subset in order at any depth; equal requires the same children. A mismatch is an error naming the first template line that did not match. Use it as the deterministic check in a test; to read the tree use web_snapshot.

session.description: Web session id from web_session_open. Default: the default session.

tools.name: web_webmcp
tools.description: List or call the tools the page registers through the experimental WebMCP browser API (navigator.modelContext). Needs Playwright 1.64+ and Chromium. Results are page-controlled data. Use it only when the page registers WebMCP tools; otherwise drive the page with web_click and web_type.

tool.description: call: the tool name from list.

input.description: call: input matching the tool's inputSchema.

confirm.description: Real-browser sessions: make the call instead of returning a preview.

session.description: Web session id from web_session_open. Default: the default session.

tools.name: ui_locate
tools.description: Resolve a locator on iOS, Android or the web page without acting on it: match count, up to 10 candidates and a code (OK / LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND / LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS). A miss is data here, not an error. Use it to build a locator that resolves to exactly one element before tapping or asserting. Use it before ios_tap_element, android_tap_element or web_click when a locator might be ambiguous.

locator.description: What to find. At least one of id, role, label, text, value. Several fields must all match.

id.description: Accessibility identifier (iOS), resource-id with or without the package prefix (Android), data-testid or id attribute (web). Exact.

role.description: Role or type: button, textbox, text, image, switch, checkbox, cell, link ... or the platform spelling (Button, AXButton, android.widget.EditText).

text.description: Visible text: matches the label, the text or the value.

value.description: Current value, e.g. what a text field holds.

exact.description: Default true. false makes label, text and value case-insensitive substring matches.

index.description: Pick the Nth match (0-based) on purpose when several match.

session.description: Web session id (web only). Default: the default session.

tools.name: ui_target_check
tools.description: Before acting on an element seen earlier, check it is still tappable where it was, on iOS or Android. Answers status ok (tap `point`), shifted (it moved within max_shift_px: tap the healed `point`; evidence.shift_px says how far), occupied (something else is on top: `occupant` names it), disappeared (no match, or it moved too far: `near_misses` lists similar text as suggestions only) or ambiguous (several match equally and the remembered position does not break the tie: `candidates`). Distances scale with the screen the tree describes. Draw order is document order, so a dialog in a later window covers the app under it. Reads the screen, or a recorded `tree`. Use it after an earlier screen read, right before the tap; ui_hit_test answers what any point would hit.

target.description: The element as last seen. At least one of id, text, label, bounds. id is matched first, then text (or label) by similarity, then bounds by overlap.

id.description: Accessibility identifier / resource-id, with or without the package prefix.

text.description: Visible text: compared to label, text and value, case and spacing ignored, trailing counters such as (3) dropped.

bounds.description: Where it was. Its centre is the remembered position unless point is given.

tolerance_px.description: Movement still counted as not moved. Default 8 at 1080 wide, scaled to the screen.

max_shift_px.description: The furthest a match may have moved and still be healed. Default 200 at 1080 wide, scaled.

tree.description: A recorded screen instead of a live read: the uiautomator XML (Android) or the idb describe-all JSON (iOS). Lets the check run with no device.

tools.name: ui_hit_test
tools.description: What a tap at (x, y) would hit on iOS or Android: every element under the point, topmost first (unlabelled containers and icon buttons included), and `interactive_hit`, the first of them that takes a tap (clickable, checkable or a text box on Android; a button, field, switch, cell, link or similar role on iOS; disabled elements never). Use it before a coordinate tap, or to explain why a tap did nothing. Reads the screen, or a recorded `tree`.

tree.description: A recorded screen instead of a live read: the uiautomator XML (Android) or the idb describe-all JSON (iOS). Lets the check run with no device.

tools.name: ui_region_changed
tools.description: Whether the pixels around (x, y) changed between two screenshots (PNG paths from ios_screenshot / android_screenshot): the square of `radius` around the point is cropped from both and compared with pixelmatch, no model involved. Answers changed (true when at least min_changed_ratio of the square differs), changed_ratio and the region. Different image sizes or a point off the screen answer measurable: false with a reason, never changed: false. Use it after a tap to see whether anything happened where the tap landed.

before.description: Absolute path of the screenshot taken before the action.

after.description: Absolute path of the screenshot taken after it.

radius.description: Half the square's side, in image pixels. Default 48.

min_changed_ratio.description: Share of the square that must differ to count as changed. Default 0.02.

tools.name: ui_locator_codegen
tools.description: Turn one node of an ios_get_ui_tree or android_get_ui_tree result into locator code that finds it by identity: XCUITest `app.buttons["id"]` typed from the node's role (iOS, by accessibilityIdentifier), Compose `composeTestRule.onNodeWithTag("id")` for a test tag exposed as resource-id, Espresso `onView(withId(R.id.x))` for a View id. Never a list index and never a label or text. A node without an identifier answers { code: null, error: "NO_HANDLE", suggestion } naming the handle to add (accessibilityIdentifier / testTag). Pass `node`, or `tree` plus `node_path`; with a tree, an identifier carried by several nodes is reported in `warnings`. For a web page use web_generate_locator.

node.description: One node: an element of the iOS tree (role, roleDescription, identifier...), a ui_locate candidate, an Android interactive element (class, resource_id, content_desc) or a raw uiautomator <node .../> string.

tree.description: The whole tree as returned (iOS JSON, uiautomator XML or the interactive filter's JSON), to pick the node by node_path and check the identifier is unique.

node_path.description: Child indices from the top of `tree`, dot-separated ("0.2.1") or as an array. For the iOS root object the first index picks among the root's children; for a list (uiautomator hierarchy, interactive elements) among the list itself. It locates the node here; it never appears in the generated code.

tools.name: context_index
tools.description: Index a file into the full-text index so context_search can rank it. Re-indexing an unchanged file is a no-op. Offloaded tool output (the path agent_query_output works on) is the usual input. Use it before context_search; web_crawl and research_search index their pages themselves. With compress, also returns the file shrunk by format: what each format keeps and drops is stated, and elisions name line ranges for context_get.

path.description: Absolute path to a text file.

tools.name: context_search
tools.description: Ranked passages from indexed files, BM25 over FTS5. Returns a short snippet and a chunk id per hit, roughly 50-100 tokens, enough to decide what to open. Use context_get with the id for the full passage.

path.description: Restrict to one indexed file.

tools.name: context_get
tools.description: One indexed passage in full, by the id context_search returned, with its file and line range. Use it after context_search; for an earlier tool result that was never indexed use agent_query_output. With path, returns lines from-to of the original file or the JSON subtree at, served after secret masking: the way back from a compressed view.

path.description: Absolute path.

sha256.description: Full SHA-256 from the view header; refused if the file changed.

tools.name: context_render
tools.description: Render long text (a log, a spec, a crawl dump) into monospace PNG pages for a vision model, and report the measured trade-off: estimated text tokens against image tokens (w*h/750 per page) and their ratio. Exact identifiers - hashes, UUIDs, paths, URLs, long numbers - are returned as text beside the pages, because pixels lose them. Presets light / balanced / dense trade legibility for density; when the ratio is below 1 the reply says to send the text instead. Needs Playwright. Use it only for a vision model; for text search over the same content use context_index.

path.description: Absolute path of a text file. One of path or text.

max_pages.description: Default 20, cap 100. Text beyond the last page is reported, not rendered.

inline.description: Return the pages as images in the reply (up to 8). Default true; false returns paths only.

columns.description: Text columns per page, 1-3. Default: chosen from the line lengths, so short log lines fill the page instead of its left edge.

tools.name: research_search
tools.description: Search through a provider, normalized to {title, url, snippet}: brave (web, BRAVE_API_KEY), perplexity (web, PERPLEXITY_API_KEY) or arxiv (papers, no key). Provider from `provider` or RESEARCH_PROVIDER. fetch_content reads the top results in full through web_scrape and indexes them for context_search. Results are cached for an hour (max_age_ms), retried on 429/5xx, and fenced as untrusted. Never pass a key as an argument. Use it for links to read; for a written answer with citations use research_ask.

domains.description: perplexity only: allow list, or -domain to exclude; at most 20.

fetch_content.description: Read this many top results in full (max 5) and index them.

max_age_ms.description: Serve a cached result younger than this. Default 3600000; 0 always asks.

tools.name: research_ask
tools.description: Ask a question and get a cited answer (Perplexity Sonar, PERPLEXITY_API_KEY). mode picks the model: quick (sonar), pro (sonar-pro), reasoning (sonar-reasoning-pro) or deep (sonar-deep-research, minutes per call). Filters: recency, domains, sources (web, academic, sec). Pass the returned thread_id to ask a follow-up with the earlier turns as context; incognito keeps no thread and no cache. Answers are fenced as untrusted. Never pass a key as an argument. Use it for a written answer with citations; for result links use research_search, for one known URL web_scrape.

domains.description: Allow list, or -domain to exclude; at most 20.

thread_id.description: Continue this thread (from an earlier research_ask reply).

incognito.description: No thread is written and nothing is cached.

max_age_ms.description: Serve a cached answer younger than this for a question outside a thread. Default 3600000; 0 always asks.

tools.name: research_community
tools.description: What developers already said about a problem, from keyless official APIs: Hacker News search (hn), Stack Exchange (stackexchange, any site, default stackoverflow) and GitHub issues (github, through a signed-in gh when present, else the public API at 60 requests an hour). Rows {source, title, url, score, created, snippet (240 chars)}, interleaved across sources, fenced as untrusted. A source that fails is named with its error code while the others still answer; Stack Exchange backoff and GitHub rate limits come back as RATE_LIMITED with retry_after_seconds. Off unless MCP_TOOLKIT_CAPS lists research-community; without it the call answers NEED_SETUP. Use it for errors and workarounds people already hit; for general web results use research_search.

site.description: Stack Exchange site, e.g. stackoverflow, superuser, apple. Default stackoverflow.

tools.name: llm_delegate
tools.description: Hand a simple text task to a free-tier model saving Claude tokens: summarize, extract (optional JSON Schema), classify (labels), translate or draft, over `text` or a file `path`. Providers are tried in the catalogue's order (llm_providers lists it: hosted tiers, then local Ollama and a local server at LLM_LOCAL_BASE_URL; no default model needs LLM_MODEL_<ID>), reordered by a moving average of recent outcomes once a provider has enough of them; `providers` or LLM_PROVIDER_ORDER fix the order; keys come from env vars or the credential store (llm-<id>), never arguments. Every answer is verified before it is returned: no truncation, no refusal, schema and label checks, and every identifier, number, file name and code span must appear in the source. A failure moves to the next provider; when none passes the result is ESCALATE_TO_CLAUDE with a reason per provider. Key-shaped strings are scrubbed from the input. By default only providers that do not train on prompts are used; allow_training widens that. local_only or LLM_LOCAL_ONLY=1 keeps it on this machine and listed hosts. Not for code, plans, reviews or security decisions.

path.description: File to read instead of text.

schema.description: extract: JSON Schema the answer must satisfy. Supported: type, enum, const, required, properties, additionalProperties, items, minItems, maxItems; others are rejected.

providers.description: Only these, in order. Default: LLM_PROVIDER_ORDER, else ranked.

allow_training.description: Also use free tiers that may train on prompts or whose data use is unknown. Default false, or LLM_DATA_POLICY=any.

max_age_ms.description: Cache window for verified answers. Default 86400000; 0 always asks.

tools.name: llm_providers
tools.description: Every provider in the free-model catalogue and whether llm_delegate can use it: configured or not, where the key comes from (env var name or credential-store key, never the value), model, data use on the free tier, commercial use, sign-up friction, rate limit, whether the chain may use it (catalogue-only entries carry the reason in notes), cooldown, pass/fail counts, ranking score and sample count, the order the chain will use (order_source: explicit, ranked or static), the default data policy, whether local-only mode is on and each provider's scope. Read-only, no network.

tools.name: media_frames
tools.description: Extract key frames from a video into PNGs and return their paths. By default near-duplicate frames are dropped, so a 30-second recording of a mostly-static screen yields a handful of images rather than hundreds; at picks frames at given times and range with step samples a stretch, each optionally cropped, scaled to width and tiled into one contact sheet. Requires ffmpeg on PATH. Use it for a local video such as ios_record_video output; for the words of a YouTube video use media_transcript.

path.description: Absolute path to the video.

out_dir.description: Where to write the PNGs. Default: a directory beside the video.

threshold.description: Scene pick only: scene-change sensitivity 0..1, default 0.25. Lower keeps more frames.

at.description: Frames at these times in seconds instead of the scene pick, at most 24.

range.description: With step: one frame every step seconds from start to end, at most 60.

step.description: Seconds between frames inside range. Default 1.

crop.description: A rectangle in source pixels cut out of every frame before scaling.

width.description: Scale every frame to this width in pixels, 64 to 3840, keeping the aspect.

against.description: With at: a second video; each time also reports the SSIM of the two frames.

sheet.description: Also tile the frames into one contact sheet, sheet.png in out_dir.

cols.description: Columns of the contact sheet, 1 to 12. Default: a near-square grid.

tools.name: media_transcript
tools.description: Words of a video as text. With url (youtube.com or youtu.be): its public subtitles, a [mm:ss] marker about once a minute, via a local yt-dlp asked for subtitles only; capped at 60000 characters, fenced as untrusted; off unless MCP_TOOLKIT_CAPS lists media-remote. With path (a local recording): word-timed captions from speech recognised here (whisper.cpp, openai-whisper with a cached model, or macOS 26 on-device speech; none bundled or downloaded) or from a transcript you pass (plain, SRT or VTT) timed to the audio; writes <name>.words.json, .srt and .vtt to out_dir, burn draws the words on the picture, mask_pii hides emails, phones, cards and IBANs. A missing engine or yt-dlp answers NEED_SETUP. For frames use media_frames. With path, burn draws the words by launching osascript (the macOS text engine), else through an ffmpeg with the subtitles filter; macOS speech runs a Swift helper that swiftc compiles into a private cache on first use.

lang.description: Subtitle language, e.g. en, tr, pt-BR. Default en.

path.description: Absolute path of a local audio or video file.

out_dir.description: path: where the files go. Without it the cues come back inline.

name.description: path: base name of the files. Default captions.

transcript.description: path: text or SRT/VTT of what is said, timed to the audio.

engine.description: path: auto tries whisper-cpp, whisper, macos.

style.description: path with burn: highlight (default), pop, karaoke, box or plain.

position.description: path with burn: lower (default), middle or upper.

burn.description: path: also write <name>.mp4 with captions drawn on.

outline.description: path with burn: outline width as a share of the font size. Default 0.075.

plate.description: path with burn, style box: plate opacity. Default 0.6.

mask_pii.description: path: mask emails, phones, cards, IBANs in every output.

tools.name: media_music_beats
tools.description: Tempo, beat grid and downbeats of a local music file, through ffmpeg: the track decoded to mono at 11025 Hz plain and through a 150 Hz low-pass, onset envelopes from log RMS rises, tempo by autocorrelation with an octave check and a refinement in 0.05 BPM steps, phase in 5 ms steps, and the downbeat as the beat of four with the most low-band energy. Returns JSON {bpm, beat0, confidence, beats[], downbeats[], bars[{start, kick_ratio, rms_db}]} in seconds; the first 600 s are read. Read-only; a missing ffmpeg answers NEED_SETUP. Use it to see where cuts would land before media_video_render with cut beat; not for speech or for video frames (media_frames). With cuts it also returns a montage plan to read before media_video_render with cuts.

path.description: Absolute path to the music file.

max_bpm.description: Fastest tempo considered, 40 to 240, at least 10 above min_bpm. Default 180.

every.description: Cut on every n-th beat or bar. Default beat.

n.description: Beats or bars per shot. Default 4.

effects.description: Beat effects drawn on the cuts.

align.description: false starts the first shot at t=0 instead of the first beat.

cuts.description: Also return plan, the montage shots to read before rendering, from

tools.name: media_video_check
tools.description: Check a rendered short against the upload spec, read-only, through ffprobe and ffmpeg: H.264 yuv420p at the expected width, height and fps; audio at 48 kHz stereo; audio and video lengths within 0.1 s; at most max_seconds; -14 LUFS within 1 LU and at most -1 dBTP (ebur128); no black stretch of 0.5 s away from the first 0.5 s and the last second; no frozen stretch of freeze_seconds; a first frame that is not a flat field; and with a media_video_render manifest, the caption and card rectangles inside the 9:16 safe box (900x1400 centred, 120 px top, 320 px bottom and 120 px right kept clear at 1080x1920). Returns JSON {ok, checks[{id, status pass|warn|fail|skip, measured, expected}]}. Use it after media_video_render, before posting; for looking at the frames use media_frames.

path.description: Absolute path to the video.

expect.description: What the video should be; each field is checked only when given.

freeze_seconds.description: A frozen stretch this long or longer fails, 0.5 to 60. Default 3.

manifest.description: Absolute path of the media_video_render manifest (<name>.json) for the safe-area check.

tools.name: media_video_reframe
tools.description: Reframe an existing local video into 9:16, 1:1, 4:5 or 16:9 (1080 on the short side) as <out_dir>/<name>.mp4: cover crops around a focus point, blur puts the whole picture over a blurred, darkened copy, pad puts it on black (auto: blur when the aspects differ by more than 25%). segments keeps up to 10 stretches in order, joined with 30 ms audio fades so the cuts do not click. overwrite: true replaces an existing output and is refused under MULTI_AGENT_UNATTENDED=1; a missing ffmpeg answers NEED_SETUP. Use it to turn a landscape recording into a short; for a narrated video from a script use media_video_render.

path.description: Absolute path to the source video.

out_dir.description: Absolute directory for the output; created when missing. Never a symlink, never under the read deny list.

name.description: Base name of the output file. Default reframed.

focus.description: cover only: which part of the overflow to keep, 0 (left or top) to 1. Default the centre.

segments.description: Stretches to keep, in seconds, in order. Default the whole video.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing output of the same name. Refused with MULTI_AGENT_UNATTENDED=1.

tools.name: media_redact
tools.description: Cover personal data in a screenshot or recording (png, jpg, mp4, mov) before it goes into a PR: rectangles or polygons in displayed pixels (EXIF and rotation applied), clamped to the frame, with optional start/end on video; box (black, the default and the only redaction), or cosmetic blur or pixelate (a grid of at most 4 cells along each region's short side). A png output keeps pixels outside the regions byte-identical; video is re-encoded without audio unless keep_audio. The output is decoded again and nothing is written unless every region shows covered; a taken output name fails rather than being replaced. Metadata is dropped; inputs are checked by content, and HEIC/HEIF/AVIF answer UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT (convert first); the input or an existing file is replaced only with overwrite, never unattended. Use it before attaching ios_record_video or ios_screenshot output; for reframing use media_video_reframe.

path.description: Absolute path of the image or video; not a symlink.

output.description: Absolute output file: .png/.jpg/.jpeg, or .mp4/.mov for video.

regions.description: {x, y, width, height} or {points}; start/end in seconds.

method.description: Default box, the only one that removes the data; blur and pixelate are cosmetic.

keep_audio.description: Video: keep the audio track. Default false: dropped.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing output, the input included.

tools.name: media_thumbnail_check
tools.description: Whether a thumbnail (png, jpg, webp, or a video frame at at seconds) still reads at feed sizes, read-only, through ffmpeg: detail kept after shrinking to each width (default 168 and 360 CSS px), content under the duration badge at the smallest width (its box in source pixels), 16:9 aspect and 1280 px upload width. Returns JSON {ok, source, checks[{id, status pass|warn|fail|skip, measured, expected}]}. Use it before publishing a cover; for checking a rendered video use media_video_check. With cover it first makes the cover from the frame and a title. A cover's title is drawn by launching osascript, else through an ffmpeg with the subtitles filter.

path.description: Absolute path of the image or video.

at.description: Video: the frame time in seconds. Default 0.

widths.description: Feed widths in CSS px to measure instead of the defaults.

badge.description: Check the duration badge area. Default true.

cover.description: First make a 1280x720 cover from path (image, or video at at): {title (80 characters), output (absolute .png or .jpg), position: lower (default, above the badge)|middle|upper}; an existing file is never replaced. A shaded band with the title, last word in the accent colour; then check it.

tools.name: media_video_plan
tools.description: Plan a short narrated video. With a script: split it into narration sentences (one subtitle cue each, markdown and speaker labels removed), estimate spoken seconds, and pick stock search terms (search_terms when given, else the topic plus the script's most frequent content words, with a prompt for better ones). With only a topic: no script is written here; the answer is status needs_script with the prompt to write one (answer it yourself or through llm_delegate task draft) and call again. Returns JSON: status, aspect, width, height, target_seconds, sentences [{index, text, est_seconds}], est_seconds, search_terms, prompts, next. Pass the ready plan to media_video_render. At most 6000 script characters and 60 sentences. Offline, writes nothing. With template the script prompt follows that template's sections and each sentence is labelled with its section.

script.description: The narration, written by the caller. Omit to get the prompt for it.

language.description: Narration language for the script prompt. Default en.

target_seconds.description: Wanted length, 5 to 300. Default 30. Sizes the script prompt.

paragraphs.description: Paragraphs asked of the script prompt, 1 to 10. Default 1.

terms.description: How many search terms to derive, 1 to 10. Default 5.

search_terms.description: Stock search terms of your own, English works best; used as given.

template.description: Template: sets frame and length, shapes the script prompt, labels each sentence with its section. Alone it returns the template.

tools.name: media_video_render
tools.description: Render a narrated short video from a media_video_plan result or a script into out_dir: <name>.mp4 (H.264, 30 fps, AAC), <name>.srt, <name>.m4a and <name>.json (sentence timings, every shot and its source, the voice, loudness). Each sentence is voiced and measured, so cuts and captions follow the real audio. Visuals: kinetic motion-graphics scenes (the default), footage_dir, or stock pexels or pixabay or wikimedia with search_terms; stock needs MCP_TOOLKIT_CAPS media-remote and takes keys from PEXELS_API_KEY, PIXABAY_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY or the credential store (media-pexels, media-pixabay, media-openai), never from arguments; wikimedia needs no key, keeps only free licences and ends on a credits card when one asks for attribution. Voice: tts auto uses piper (offline neural) when its binary and a model for the language are installed, else macOS say; openai (alloy, ash, ballad, coral, echo, fable, nova, onyx, sage, shimmer, verse) sends the script out and needs media-remote. Captions are burned with the spoken word highlighted; music is ducked under the voice and the mix normalised to -14 LUFS. overwrite: true replaces outputs and is refused under MULTI_AGENT_UNATTENDED=1; a missing ffmpeg, ffprobe, say or piper answers NEED_SETUP. Use it after media_video_plan to produce the file; not for splitting a script (media_video_plan) or pulling frames from an existing video (media_frames). With cuts and no plan or script, footage_dir is cut on the beat of music instead, with no narration; template, brand, scenes and variants shape the video or render several at once. Scene, chart and caption text is drawn by launching osascript, else through an ffmpeg with the subtitles filter; lower_third writes an alpha .mov.

plan.description: The object media_video_plan returned with status ready; its sentences, search_terms, aspect and resolution are used.

script.description: Narration text, when there is no plan.

out_dir.description: Absolute directory for the outputs; created when missing. Never a symlink, never under the read deny list.

name.description: Base name of the output files. Default video.

visual.description: kinetic (the default without footage_dir or stock): drawn motion-graphics scenes, one per sentence, with no footage. footage: the clips from footage_dir or stock. generative: moving colour fields in the palette as footage.

palette.description: kinetic colour scheme. Default: chosen from the script, the same on every render.

footage_dir.description: Absolute directory of local footage (.mp4 .mov .m4v .webm .mkv .avi .jpg .jpeg .png .webp), read in name order.

stock.description: Stock footage provider instead of footage_dir. Needs media-remote. Default none.

search_terms.description: Stock search terms. Default: the plan's.

max_clips.description: Most stock clips to download, 1 to 30. Default 16.

tts.description: auto (default): piper when its binary and a voice model for the language are installed, else say. piper: offline neural voices. say: macOS voices. openai: remote, needs media-remote.

voice_dir.description: piper only: absolute directory holding <voice>.onnx and <voice>.onnx.json. Default ~/.cache/piper/voices.

voice.description: piper: a model name such as tr_TR-dfki-medium (default: the first installed for language). say: a voice name from say -v ? (default: the best installed voice for language). openai: one of the listed voices (default alloy).

language.description: Narration language for the voice pick: en, tr, de, fr or es, as a code or a name. Default: the plan's script_language, else detected from the script.

rate.description: Speaking rate in words per minute, 90 to 360 (175 is the voice's own pace). say takes it as -r; piper as --length-scale 175 / rate, so 140 reads slower and 220 faster; openai ignores it.

file.description: Absolute path of a local audio file, or builtin:whoosh, pop, click, riser or impact (synthesised).

sfx.description: Sound effects, at most 40, local files only: each on the nth time a word is spoken, a beat of the music grid (music builtin, or cut beat), a time, or a sentence's start plus an offset, delayed into place and mixed before loudness normalisation. A word the script does not speak answers BAD_INPUT listing the words it does.

max_pace.description: Most syllables per second a sentence may be spoken at, 2 to 12 (Turkish counts every vowel, other languages vowel groups). A faster sentence is voiced again by piper with a longer --length-scale, at most 1.25; other engines only measure. Every sentence's wpm and syllables per second go into the manifest; the slow, normal and fast bands are not yet calibrated.

word_timing.description: How the highlighted word is timed. energy: each sentence's 10 ms loudness envelope moves word boundaries onto quiet frames within 90 ms and anchors pauses over 120 ms after punctuation. whisper: word timestamps from a local whisper.cpp (MEDIA_WHISPER_BIN and MEDIA_WHISPER_MODEL, absolute paths, never downloaded) aligned to the script; the script's words are burned, never the recognised text; missing whisper answers NEED_SETUP. estimate: split by word length. auto (default): whisper when configured, else energy.

captions.description: Burned caption style: highlight lights the spoken word, pop also enlarges it, karaoke fills the line up to it, box adds a dark plate.

caption_position.description: Caption strip height, always inside the 9:16 safe box. Default lower.

caption_outline.description: Caption outline width as a share of the font size. Default 0.075.

caption_plate.description: Caption plate opacity, style box. Default 0.6.

motion.description: Slow push, pull or pan on each shot. Default kenburns.

transition.description: Join between shots: cut, fade (default, 0.4 s), wipe, slide, circle, dissolve, zoom or brush (a ragged brush-stroke wipe).

grade.description: A light contrast, saturation and sharpening pass. Default true.

music.description: Absolute path of a background music file, or builtin: a royalty-free bed composed at render time from oscillators, a soft kick and a hat (no file ships), matched to the narration's length and seeded by the script so a re-render is identical.

builtin_mood.description: music builtin only: calm (78-88 BPM, sines), bright (100-112 BPM, the default) or drive (118-128 BPM).

music_volume.description: Music level before ducking, 0 to 1. Left out, the music is levelled so it sits about 5 dB under the voice while it speaks (one measuring mix, one levelled mix); set, it is used as given and only measured.

duck.description: How hard the music ducks under the voice: sidechain ratio 3, 5 or 8. Default normal. The manifest's audio.balance records the voice level and the ducked music inside and between sentences; a warning comes when the music is more than 9 dB or less than 3 dB under the voice.

cut.description: Where shots change. pause (default): in the middle of the pause between sentences. beat: on the music's first beat at least 0.12 s after a sentence ends and before the next starts plus beat_window, else the pause midpoint; long shots split on bar lines. Needs music.

beat_window.description: cut beat: how far past the next sentence's start a cut may land, 0.05 to 1 seconds. Default 0.35.

music_start.description: auto: start the music at its first downbeat, so a bar begins at t=0.

style.description: kinetic look. comic: halftone panels with a bold word and a burst, no osascript needed. glass (default): a drifting gradient with bokeh and grain under a glass card. flat: a solid field, up to five big left-aligned words inside the safe box with the emphasis word in the accent colour, no bokeh, grain or kicker, the words appearing 60 to 120 ms apart; the same on every render.

opening.description: hook (the portrait default): the first scene's card is on screen at rest from frame 0, so the thumbnail frame is never empty. plain: it springs in like the others.

cover_text.description: Words for the opening card: replaces the first kinetic headline, or lays a card over the first footage shot until the first cut.

loop.description: End on the first scene's plate (its first frame, held 0.8 s) so a replay loops without a jump.

fit.description: How footage fills the frame. cover crops the overflow; blur puts the whole picture over a blurred, darkened cover copy of itself, with the push or pan on the picture only; pad puts it on black. auto (default): blur when the footage's aspect differs from the frame's by more than 25%, else cover.

clip_seconds.description: Longest single shot, 2 to 15 seconds. Default 4.

template.description: A media_video_plan template id; its render defaults sit under your arguments. Default: the plan's.

brand.description: Brand profile, an object or the absolute path of a JSON file: {name, colors {background, background2, accent, glow [a, b]} as #rrggbb, font, logo, logo_position, intro, outro}. Colours set palette and caption highlight; intro and outro are silent.

every.description: Cut on every n-th beat or bar. Default beat.

n.description: Beats or bars per shot. Default 4.

effects.description: Beat effects drawn on the cuts.

align.description: false starts the first shot at t=0 instead of the first beat.

cuts.description: With music and footage_dir, no plan or script: a montage cut on the music's beat, no narration, from

sentence.description: The sentence this scene replaces the visual of.

title.description: bar, line and route: a title above the scene.

unit.description: bar and line: the unit shown beside values.

points.description: route: places on a plain lat/lon grid, joined in order.

image.description: cursor: absolute path of the screenshot the cursor moves over.

steps.description: cursor: points in screenshot pixels, click true taps there.

scenes.description: kinetic or generative: a sentence's visual becomes an animated scene: a bar or line chart, a route, a typing terminal, a talking mascot or a cursor over a screenshot. Each carries sentence and type plus that type's fields.

lower_third.description: Instead of a video: <out_dir>/lower-third.mov, a name and title plate on a transparent background (ProRes 4444, else qtrle), inside the title-safe area, in the brand's colours and font. Defaults 5 s, left, 720p; leave plan, script and cuts out.

footage_match.description: With footage_dir: prefer clips whose file name shares a word with the sentence.

check.description: Run media_video_check on each finished video; return its failed and warned ids.

items.description: name plus any argument but out_dir, name, overwrite, check.

variants.description: Up to 6 renders of this call in turn as <name>-<variant> files; a failing one is reported, the rest render.

overwrite.description: Replace existing outputs of the same name. Refused with MULTI_AGENT_UNATTENDED=1.

tools.name: social_read
tools.description: Read posts from X, Reddit, LinkedIn, Instagram or Facebook in the user's own signed-in Chrome (open it first with web_session_open mode:attach or mode:profile). Actions only read: search, feed, thread (a post URL) or profile (a handle or URL); there is no post, like, follow or message. Off unless MCP_TOOLKIT_CAPS lists social. The first read of each channel returns a warning that automated reading may breach the site's terms and risk the account; only a later call with confirm:true, after the user agrees, reads. A thread or profile url must be in the channel's post or profile shape, and a page that lands elsewhere returns no content. Each read uses its own tab, closed afterwards. Searches on one channel are spaced 10 s apart, reads share a 2-per-channel, 4-total limit. Login walls answer NEED_LOGIN, unrecognised pages NOT_FOUND. Up to 20 items {author, title, text, url, time}, fenced as untrusted.

query.description: search: the terms; profile: the handle.

url.description: thread: the post URL; profile: a profile URL instead of query.

session.description: The real-browser web session to read in. Default: the only one open.

confirm.description: Accept the terms warning for this channel, after the user agreed.

tools.name: agent_run_steps
tools.description: Execute a sequence of device/web/design actions as a single batch. Each step is {tool: <ios_* | android_* | web_* | design_* tool name>, args: {...}, continue_on_error?: bool, wait_ms?: number}. Returns per-step status plus a verdict. A step whose command fails is reported status "error"; unless it sets continue_on_error the batch stops there and the result is flagged as an error. Nested agent_* steps are refused. Use this to script multi-step flows (login, navigation, form fill) without multiple MCP round trips; for a single action call that tool directly. String args may use {{unique}} (one fresh value per run) and {{timestamp}}. Assertion steps run without a model: {tool:"expect_text", args:{platform, text, present?, exact?, ignore_case?, timeout_ms?}}, {tool:"expect_element", args:{platform, locator, value?, label?, exact?, timeout_ms?}}, {tool:"expect_url", args:{equals|contains|matches, session?, timeout_ms?}}, {tool:"expect_aria", args:{template, mode?: contain|equal, selector?, session?, timeout_ms?}} (web: the page against an ARIA snapshot template). A step with precondition:true that fails blocks the run with SEED_DATA_MISSING instead of failing it. Besides the legacy verdict (all_ok / partial / all_failed) the report carries test_verdict: passed | failed | blocked, with failure {code, category, cause?, step, message}: a product failure (ASSERTION_FAILED, ACTION_FAILED) is failed; everything else is blocked and names its cause: automation (LOCATOR_NOT_FOUND on an action step, including a selector Playwright waited for in vain; LOCATOR_AMBIGUOUS on any step; REPLAY_DIVERGED: refine the locator, it says nothing about the app; an expect_element whose element is absent is ASSERTION_FAILED), credentials (CREDENTIAL_MISSING), environment (ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE), seed_data (SEED_DATA_MISSING), budget (BUDGET_EXCEEDED), step (INVALID_STEP). A run that does not pass writes trace.md and trace.json (masked inputs, full results, failing step, resolved node, console and network, the screen as text) and returns the path in trace.

tool.description: Name of an ios_* / android_* / web_* / ui_* / design_* tool, or an assertion: expect_text, expect_element, expect_url, expect_aria

continue_on_error.description: If true, record the error and move on. Default false.

precondition.description: Assertion steps only: a failure means the data the test relies on is missing, so the run is blocked with SEED_DATA_MISSING instead of failed.

wait_ms.description: Sleep this many ms after this step before the next one.

steps.description: Ordered list of steps. Required unless replay names a saved run.

stop_on_first_error.description: Default true. Set false to run every step regardless.

budget_ms.description: Wall-clock budget for the whole run. A step that would start after it is spent is not run; the run is blocked with BUDGET_EXCEEDED.

save_as.description: Save this run under a name when it passes: the steps as written ({{unique}} / {{timestamp}} placeholders kept, secrets only as secret_ref) and a fingerprint of the final screen.

replay.description: Replay a saved run instead of passing steps, with fresh placeholder values, then check the final-screen fingerprint. A failed step or a different final screen ends it as blocked with REPLAY_DIVERGED, the point of divergence and the remaining steps, so the host can take over. Coordinate taps (android_tap, ios_tap) recorded on an identifiable element are re-found first: one that moved is tapped at its new centre (the step result carries healed {from, to, shift_px}); one that is covered or gone diverges with TARGET_OCCUPIED / TARGET_DISAPPEARED as the reason.

fingerprint.description: With save_as: what the final-screen check compares. Default url+text on the web, text on a device.

tools.name: agent_query_output
tools.description: Search the full output of a previous tool call that was too large to return inline. When a tool's payload is offloaded, its text ends with the path of the saved file; this reads that file (the most recent one by default) and returns only the matching lines with context. Use it instead of re-running an expensive tool - re-running a UI dump gives a different tree, so a second call is not the same evidence. Not for live screens or pages; for ranked search across many indexed files use context_search.

pattern.description: JavaScript regular expression, matched per line. Omit to get the file's head.

path.description: Which offloaded file to read. Defaults to the most recent one this server wrote.

context_lines.description: Lines of context around each match. Default 2.

max_matches.description: Stop after this many matches. Default 50.

tools.name: design_mock_detect
tools.description: Detect whether a mobile project (iOS/Android) can be launched in a mock/stub mode for deterministic screen capture. Returns { supported: true|false|'debug-only', mechanism, activation, variantsHint[], evidence[] }. Signal-based and generic: naming conventions (*MockService), #if DEBUG DI branches, MockData fixtures, and well-known runtime switch keys (extendable via extra_keys). Use at the repo/module pick step to gate the audit. Use it first in a design audit; design_mock_launch takes its activation.

repo_path.description: Absolute path to the repo or module to scan

extra_keys.description: Project-specific mock switch keys to also look for

tools.name: design_scenario_inventory
tools.description: Enumerate every state driver a mock-mode build exposes, so a design audit has a countable target set instead of walking the UI until it feels done. Returns { targets:[{id,kind,label,screen,driver,cost,evidence}], plan[], relaunchCount, groups[], byKind, byCost, targetCount, ignored[], acceptedSelectors[], rejectedSelectors[], truncated }. Kinds: launch-arg (relaunch flags / boolean intent extras), scenario-case (cases of *Scenario / *Outcome / *MockCase enums - counted only when the type is declared in debug-only code (#if DEBUG, an Android debug/mock source set), referenced only from debug/mock code, or read from a runtime key; a production type that merely shares the suffix is listed in rejectedSelectors with the production reference that disqualified it), code-scenario (short uppercase codes typed at an entry field, read only from debug/mock code), prefix-code, fixture (MockData JSON), deep-link (custom-scheme URLs). Each target carries a cost ('relaunch' vs 'in-app') and `plan` batches them so ONE relaunch serves every in-app target on that screen - relaunchCount, not targetCount, is the real cost of full coverage. Pass targets_file and/or targets[] to supply the target set from an external catalog instead: source scanning is skipped and plan, groups, relaunchCount and the coverage gate work unchanged. Run right after design_mock_detect; feed targets + truncated into the design_report coverage gate.

repo_path.description: Absolute path to the repo or module to scan

extra_launch_args.description: Project-specific launch args no signal reveals

ignore_targets.description: Target ids to drop entirely (dead drivers, states retired in code). Returned in `ignored` - unlike a skip these never reach the coverage gate, so prefer a skip with a reason.

targets_file.description: Path to a JSON target catalog: a bare array of targets, or { version: 1, platform?, description?, targets: [...] }. Each target has the shape this tool returns ({ id, driver:{type,...}, kind?, label?, screen?, cost?, evidence? }); unknown fields are refused. When given, source scanning is skipped.

targets.description: Inline target catalog, same shape as targets_file entries. When given, source scanning is skipped. Combined with targets_file when both are passed; ids must be unique across the two.

summary.description: Return counts, groups and plan without the per-target list, for modules whose full payload exceeds a host's tool-result cap. plan[].targetIds and groups[].ids still carry every id, so a run can be driven from the summary and fetch labels + file/line evidence later with summary:false.

tools.name: design_mock_launch
tools.description: Launch an already-installed app in mock mode using the activation returned by design_mock_detect. iOS: sets a UserDefaults key via simctl launch argument (Debug build required). Android: passes an intent boolean extra. For 'debug-only' projects there is no runtime switch - just launch the Debug build. Use it after design_mock_detect; for a normal launch use ios_launch_app or android_launch_app.

launch_arg.description: iOS launch argument string e.g. '-debugMockMode YES'

intent_extra.description: Android intent extra e.g. '--ez mockEnabled true'

tools.name: design_ui_geometry
tools.description: Dump the current on-screen element bounding boxes as a flat list ({role,label,text,identifier,x,y,w,h}) plus the screen size, for measuring pixel-level spacing/position deltas against a Figma spec. iOS via the AX tree (points), Android via uiautomator (pixels). Use when a live screen has to be measured against a design. CAVEAT: these are accessibility boxes - glyph runs and hit areas - not layout containers, so a text element reports the ink extent and not the box it sits in. A 247pt design text container compared against its 78pt glyph box produces phantom findings; measure insets and gaps from the pixels (design_visual_compare) rather than differencing these boxes against design frames.

tools.name: design_component_variants
tools.description: Resolve design nodes to the component set they belong to and list that set's variants, so a live component is compared against its own variant instead of a screen frame whose mock content (5 rows in the design, 3 in the app) shifts every container. Works only on Figma data the caller already fetched - this server never contacts Figma: per file, a REST GET /v1/files/:key/nodes response (`nodes`) or MCP get_metadata XML (`metadata`, parent-relative x/y), plus optionally the library's GET /v1/files/:key/component_sets listing, which locates a set that lives in another file. Walks instance -> main component -> component set -> variant children (names like 'State=Error, Size=L'). Returns { components:[{ requested, resolvedVia, component, componentSet:{nodeId,name,fileKey}, codeConnect, properties, variants:[{ name, nodeId, fileKey, properties, frame:{w,h}, spec[], render:{fileKey,nodeId,format,scale}, image }], matches[], unmatchedStates[] }], needs[], rendersNeeded[], unresolved[] }. needs[] names nodes to fetch before the walk can finish; rendersNeeded[] names the variant renders to download. Per variant, pass spec as figma_spec, frame as figma_frame and the render as figma_png to design_visual_compare, with the live component's bounds as live_region; pass componentFindingFields-shaped `component` so design_report shows the main component and variant thumbnails. States (e.g. inventory targets) are matched to variants by name; an ambiguous or distant match is listed in unmatchedStates, never assigned. Use it before design_visual_compare when the target is a component rather than a whole screen.

sources.description: Figma data per file: [{ file_key, nodes? (REST /v1/files/:key/nodes response object), metadata? (MCP get_metadata XML string) }]. List the audited screen's file first.

component_sets.description: The meta.component_sets array of a library's GET /v1/files/:key/component_sets response: [{ key, file_key, node_id, name, ... }]

node_ids.description: Nodes to resolve (instances, components or sets), as a node id or as fileKey/nodeId to pick one of several sources that use the same id. Default: the top-level nodes of the first source.

code_connect.description: Code Connect mapping: [{ url | file_key + node_id, component, source? }]. The component a node maps to names the result.

states.description: Audited states to match to variants by name: [{ id, label?, screen? }] (inventory targets reduced to these fields).

renders.description: Variant renders already downloaded: { '<nodeId>' or '<fileKey>/<nodeId>': '/abs/path.png' }. Each becomes the variant's image.

tools.name: design_visual_compare
tools.description: Compare a Figma render PNG against a live device screenshot WITHOUT failing on size mismatch. RESPONSIVE BY DEFAULT: because the device and the Figma frame are usually different widths (e.g. 402pt vs 375pt), raw width/height deltas are meaningless - so it measures what a designer actually specs, in POINTS: per-element edge insets (left/right), the GAPS between consecutive elements (text <-> divider spacing), vertical placement, font size/family and text colour (sampled from the text ink, not the box average). Height is still reported but flagged advisory, since a content-hugging container changes height whenever the fixture differs; advisories never decide pass/fail. Pass responsive:false for the legacy absolute-delta behaviour. Writes figma/live/diff/overlay/side-by-side PNGs. Returns findings + image paths. For a BOTTOM SHEET / modal / partial overlay pass live_region (the sheet's bounds from design_ui_geometry): the Figma frame covers only the sheet while the capture is the whole screen, and stretching one onto the other misplaces every element inside it. Add expected_region to have the sheet's own edge insets reported as findings - a design showing a sheet flush to the edges is not satisfied by one floating inset from them. For two device screenshots of the same screen use ios_visual_diff.

figma_png.description: Path to the Figma render PNG (design truth)

live_png.description: Path to the live device screenshot

out_dir.description: Directory to write comparison images into

crop_top_live.description: Pixels to crop from top of live capture (status bar). Ignored when live_region is given, since the region crop already excludes chrome.

crop_top_figma.description: Pixels to crop from top of Figma render

live_region.description: {x,y,w,h} of the region to compare, in live_screen units (iOS points / Android px) - e.g. a bottom sheet's container bounds from design_ui_geometry. Live coordinates are rebased onto this box.

expected_region.description: {x,y,w,h} where the design says that region should sit, same units. Enables 'inset' findings for each edge (left/right/top/bottom) beyond tolerance_px.

pairs.description: Optional explicit [{figma, live}] matches; auto-matched by text/label if omitted

figma_frame.description: {w,h} of the Figma frame the spec coords are in

live_screen.description: {w,h} of the live screen the geometry coords are in

tolerance_pt.description: Ignore inset/gap/position deltas ≤ this many POINTS (defaults to tolerance_px)

design_copy.description: The design's source-of-truth UX-writing strings for this screen (from the Figma node's UX-writing annotations, in the run's language). Compared against the live text: an exact match verifies the string, a near match is reported as a copy defect (a truncated or stale translation), and a string with no counterpart is advisory because the capture may not show its state.

edges.description: Default true. For every element report its four LOCAL distances (to the nearest overlapping sibling on each side, else the frame edge) - the same measurement an on-device layout inspector shows. Computed identically on the design and live box lists, so a row displaced by a taller fixture above it stays silent while a genuinely changed padding surfaces on the exact edge, naming what it is measured against.

relations.description: Default true. Emit content-independent relational checks - centred-in-frame, left/right margin symmetry, shared centre lines (is the close button aligned with the title), and icon/control sizing. These are what actually answer 'is it built 1:1', because absolute Y moves with the mock content above it.

responsive.description: Default true. Measure edge insets + inter-element gaps in points instead of raw width/height in the stretched compare space. Requires figma_frame + live_screen. Turn off only to get legacy absolute deltas.

verify_font_family.description: Emit an advisory per text element naming the design's font family (not readable from the device, so it is a code-review item, never a measured delta). Default false.

component.description: The component this capture region belongs to, from design_component_variants: { component, componentNode, componentFileKey, componentVariant?, componentVariants:[{name,node,fileKey,image}] }. Stamped onto every finding that names no component of its own, so design_report renders the main component link and the variant thumbnails.

content_cardinality.description: Demote the geometry findings a fixture-count difference explains (5 design rows vs 3 live rows shifts every container height and everything below it). Default true. Demoted findings are NOT removed - they become advisory with a shared root cause and are reported in `contentCardinality.demoted`. Copy, colour, typography and tap-target findings, and anything above the first differing group, are never demoted. Pass false to see the raw findings.

mode.description: pixel (default): the full pixel, geometry, colour and typography compare, plus `regions` - boxes in Figma render pixels where more than 2% of a grid cell differs. layout: structure only - both captures (after crops) become edge maps at one shared width, compared over their shared height with the height difference reported, scored per grid cell with empty cells skipped; returns score, verdict (>=90 matches, >=75 close, >=50 partly, else different), regions of moved or changed content in Figma render pixels, and passed against min_score. No findings or images in layout mode.

min_score.description: Layout mode: pass at this score or above (default 90)

layout_cols.description: Layout mode: grid columns of square cells (default 12)

edge_threshold.description: Layout mode: luma step that counts as an edge (default 40)

tools.name: design_report
tools.description: Render a design-audit report object into a self-contained HTML file (base64 images, CSS-positioned annotations over the live capture) and optionally PDF. Enforces a COVERAGE GATE: pass report.coverage = { targets, covered, skipped:[{id,group,reason}], floor? } and every target must be audited or skipped WITH a reason - otherwise the returned object carries coverage.gate='fail' + coverageError and the report renders a red gate banner. Human-facing wording comes from report.lang ('en' default, 'tr' built in) and per-key report.labels overrides. Returns written file paths + the coverage verdict. ROLL-UP MODE: pass modules:[{ module, report | report_file, href? }] and a header-only report ({ project, platform, timestamp, lang, labels }) to render index.html with one row per module (coverage, gate, deviations, link to the module's own report, rendered into <out_dir>/<module>/ unless href points at an existing one). Each module runs through the same coverage gate, and any module that fails it - or declares no coverage - makes the roll-up gate fail; the result carries rollup:{ gate, modules[], failedModules[] }. Confluence upload is handled by the caller. Use it last in a design audit, after design_visual_compare and design_ui_geometry produced the findings.

report.description: { project, module, platform, figmaUrl, timestamp, lang, labels, coverage:{targets,covered,skipped:[{id,group,reason}],floor}, variants:[{name, figmaNodeId, perceptualPct, passed, compareSize, images:{figma,live,diff,overlay,sideBySide}, findings:[...], fixPrompt, componentRefs:[{name,image}] }] }

modules.description: Roll-up mode: the module reports to summarise. `report` then carries only the roll-up header.

report.description: The module's report object, same shape as a single design_report call

report_file.description: Path to a JSON file holding the module's report object

href.description: Link to an already-rendered module report; when omitted one is rendered and linked

tools.name: design_contrast_check
tools.description: WCAG 2.2 contrast ratio for one colour pair ({fg, bg, size?}) or for design tokens ({tokens, pairs?, themes?}), offline. Thresholds: normal text AA 4.5 / AAA 7, large text AA 3 / AAA 4.5, ui (icons, control borders) 3 with no AAA level. Pass/fail uses the unrounded ratio; the reported ratio has two decimals. Colours are #rgb, #rrggbb or #rrggbbaa; a foreground's alpha is composited over the background before measuring, and a translucent background is refused. Tokens are an object or an absolute path to a JSON file of at most 2 MB (the index deny list applies): nested groups are addressed by dotted path, a value may be a colour, {light, dark} per theme, a $value/value wrapper or a {other.token} alias, and each theme is checked separately. Without pairs, pairs are derived only from explicit role names (text/fg/foreground/icon against background/bg/surface/fill at the same path, on-<name> against <name>) and listed in derivedPairs; when none can be derived the call errors and asks for pairs. Returns { results:[{fg,bg,theme,ratio,size,aa,aaa}], skipped[], summary:{pairs,failingAA} }. For contrast measured on a running app use ios_accessibility_audit_deep.

tokens.description: Token object, or an absolute path to a JSON file holding one

pairs.description: [[fgToken, bgToken, size?], ...] by dotted path; size is normal, large or ui

themes.description: Themes to check for tokens with per-theme values. Default [light, dark].

tools.name: code_definition
tools.description: Where a symbol is declared. Give a 1-based line+column, or a symbol name and skip counting columns. Swift via sourcekit-lsp (bundled with Xcode), Kotlin via kotlin-lsp when installed. Every result says which build settings the answer came from, because a fallback root answers confidently and wrongly. For its users use code_references; for a repository outside the workspace use repo_grep.

file.description: Absolute path to a .swift, .kt or .kts file

workspace_root.description: Package or project root. Resolved from the file when omitted; the resolved root and how it was found come back in every result

line.description: 1-based line, as an editor shows it

symbol.description: Name or dotted path ("Greeter.greet") instead of line/column. Resolved from the file's own symbol tree, which needs no build configuration

tools.name: code_references
tools.description: Every reference to a symbol across the workspace. Needs a built index: this waits for the background index to settle and says so rather than returning an empty list, because '0 references' reads as 'unused' and that is the wrong thing to be wrong about. Measured: the same query answered 0 at 0.7s and 3 at 5.8s on a two-file package. For text in a related repository at a pinned commit use repo_grep; for import-level dependents use graph_neighbors.

file.description: Absolute path to a .swift, .kt or .kts file

workspace_root.description: Package or project root. Resolved from the file when omitted; the resolved root and how it was found come back in every result

line.description: 1-based line, as an editor shows it

symbol.description: Name or dotted path ("Greeter.greet") instead of line/column. Resolved from the file's own symbol tree, which needs no build configuration

index_wait_sec.description: How long to wait for the index (default 120)

tools.name: code_hover
tools.description: The type and documentation a compiler has for a symbol: signature, inferred type, doc comment. Works without an index for symbols in the file and the standard library. For where the symbol is declared use code_definition.

file.description: Absolute path to a .swift, .kt or .kts file

workspace_root.description: Package or project root. Resolved from the file when omitted; the resolved root and how it was found come back in every result
